findings.title: No task updates `config_to_yaml`; adding the enum field breaks existing YAML tests and success criterion 5
findings.description:
Tasks 1.2 and 1.3 (lines 59–76) add a `BoundsPolicy` field. Task 1.4 (line 88) adds a round-trip test, but no task changes `config_to_yaml`. The plan relies on the slice's claim (slice lines 224–227) that "`StrEnum` subclasses `str` so `yaml.dump` will serialize it as a plain string automatically". That claim is wrong:
- `yaml.dump` uses the full `Representer`. It looks up representers by exact type, so a `BoundsPolicy` value falls through to the `object` multi-representer.
- That produces `!!python/object/apply:migratory_server.config.BoundsPolicy [...]`, which `yaml.safe_load` in `load()` (config.py:630) rejects.

This happens even under the `OPEN` default, because `dataclasses.asdict` always emits the field. As a result, two existing tests fail as soon as Task 1.2 lands: `TestConfigToYaml.test_output_is_valid_yaml` (tests/test_config.py:767-771, which calls `yaml.safe_load`) and `test_roundtrip_basic_config` (tests/test_config.py:773-785). The Section 1 commit at line 96 would therefore sit at a failing point.

The current code fixed this with `_serialize_for_yaml` (config.py:657-669), which no task describes. Task 1.3 needs a step that converts `StrEnum` values to `.value` before `yaml.dump`. The slice's claim at lines 224–227 should also be corrected.

findings.title: Task 3.4 integration tests are missing, though the file says `status: complete`; success criteria 10 and 11 are unverified
findings.description:
Line 9 says `status: complete`, and Task 5.3 (line 313) asserts the work is complete. But a search for `TestBoundsPolicyIntegration`, `test_open_policy_does_not_call_enforcement`, `test_wrap_policy_keeps_all_positions_inside`, `test_reflect_policy_flips_velocities_at_edges` and `drift_out_of_bounds` finds them only in the task file itself. Nothing in `tests/` calls `apply_bounds_policy` from `SimulationManager.step`, and nothing asserts that the `OPEN` path skips the call.

That leaves two criteria with no test at all:
- **Success criterion 10:** the call happens when the policy isn't `OPEN` and is skipped (verified by a spy) when it is.
- **Success criterion 11:** the 50-tick integration test across `OPEN`, `WRAP` and `REFLECT`.

Every checkbox in the file is still `[ ]`. Either Task 3.4 needs to be done, or the status has to go back to in-progress.

findings.title: Task 3.4 test inputs are underspecified; the reflect test as written would fail with the existing fixtures
findings.description:
`test_reflect_policy_flips_velocities_at_edges` (line 231) puts an agent at `(99, 50)` with velocity `(10, 0)`, takes one step, and asserts `vx < 0`. It doesn't say what `dt` or `max_speed` to use.

With the file's existing fixtures (`_profile` gives `max_speed=5.0`, and every existing construction uses `dt=0.05`), the engine clamps speed to 5 (src/migratory/engine/integration.py:23,43). The agent then moves to x = 99.25, never crosses 100, and `vx` stays positive, so the assertion fails.

The `OPEN` drift test (line 228) has the same issue: over 50 steps an agent travels at most 5 × 0.05 × 50 = 12.5 units, so "near the edges" (line 226) has to mean within 12.5 units. The task should state concrete values, for example `dt=1.0` with `max_speed ≥ 10` and starting positions within a few units of each edge.

findings.title: `np.mod` wrap can return exactly `width`, which breaks the half-open interval in success criterion 7
findings.description:
Task 2.2 (line 134) and Note line 330 say `np.mod` produces values in `[0, width)`. That isn't true in floating point. For tiny negative values, Python-style modulo rounds to the divisor: `np.mod(-1e-17, 100.0) == 100.0`. So an agent that steps just past the left edge lands on `x == width`, which violates success criterion 7 ("half-open … for arbitrarily large overshoot"). The `WRAP` integration test at line 229 (`x < width`) could also fail intermittently.

Task 2.2 should add a post-step (for example `positions[positions[:,0] >= width, 0] = 0.0`), and Task 2.3 should add a `test_wrap_tiny_negative` case.

findings.title: `**Commit:**` markers are checkboxes inside their own tasks
findings.description: The commit markers at lines 96, 179, 249, 286 and 325 are written as `- [ ] **Commit:** ...`, and each sits in a separate "Task N.x: Commit" (1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3, 5.5). Commit markers should be plain lines, never checkboxes. The fix is to turn each into a plain `**Commit**:` line at the end of the test task before it (1.4, 2.3, 3.5, 4.2, 5.4) and delete the five commit-only tasks. Where they are placed — once per section, after testing — is fine.

findings.title: Manual walkthrough edits the shipped `config/test.yaml`; an interrupted run leaves success criterion 12 broken with nothing to catch it
findings.description:
Task 5.2 steps 6–8 (lines 304–306) edit the tracked `config/test.yaml` to `reflect` and then `open`, and step 8 asks the user to restore it. Task 5.5 (line 324) stages only docs.

If the walkthrough stops after step 6 or 7, or the user restores the wrong value, the tree is left dirty with a non-`wrap` shipped config. Only a person editing the file can undo that:
- No test pins `test.yaml`'s policy. The only shipped-config test loads `default.yaml` (tests/test_config.py:44-45).
- Neither Task 4.1 nor 4.2 adds such a test.

Steps 6–7 should use a scratch copy (for example `cp config/test.yaml /tmp/313-reflect.yaml`, edit that, and pass `--config /tmp/...`). Alternatively, add a test asserting both shipped configs load with `BoundsPolicy.WRAP`, which would also give success criterion 12 automated coverage.

findings.title: Task 3.1's "required keyword argument" has no position specified and no longer matches the code
findings.description:
Task 3.1 (line 186) says to add `world_bounds` as a required argument but doesn't say where.

- **If it goes after `environment: Environment | None = None`:** a non-default argument after a default one is a `SyntaxError`, unless it is made keyword-only with `*`.
- **If it goes before `environment`:** it works, but every existing construction must change. The 22 constructions in tests/test_simulation.py (137–573), none of which pass `world_bounds`, are covered by Task 3.4 line 233.

The current code went a different way: `world_bounds: WorldBoundsConfig | None = None`, falling back to `entity_manager.world_bounds` (simulation.py:64,72-76). That contradicts Task 3.1's success criterion ("requires `world_bounds`", line 191) and the slice (line 272). The task should name the parameter's position and decide between required and optional with a fallback. The plan and the slice should match whichever is chosen.

findings.title: Stale or wrong claims about existing code
findings.description:
- Task 1.1 (line 46) puts `WorldBoundsConfig` at line 25. It is now at config.py:47.
- Task 1.1 (line 47) says to add `from enum import StrEnum`. That import already exists at config.py:7, so following the step literally would duplicate it.
- Task 1.3 (line 69) says `_validate_world_bounds` is "around line 156". It is at config.py:180.
- Task 1.4 (line 80) refers to a `TestWorldBounds` class. No such class exists. The policy tests live in `TestRangeValidation` (tests/test_config.py:139, 172–219), so the task's "nearest equivalent" fallback covers this.
- Task 3.5 (line 241) lists `tests/test_clients.py` as a possible `SimulationManager` caller. It isn't one. The callers outside `test_simulation.py` are tests/test_force_builder.py:201 and tests/test_repulsor_integration.py:53.
- Task 2.3's "all three policies" parametrize (line 171) and Task 2.1's three-way `match` (lines 120–123) predate `BoundsPolicy.SOFT` (config.py:23, added in slice 314). The dispatch now also handles `SOFT` (bounds_enforcement.py:41-42).

findings.title: Task 2.2's inactive-tail guarantee has no test
findings.description: Task 2.2's success criterion (line 143) says the helpers "do not touch the inactive tail of arrays passed as `[:count]` views". No test in Task 2.3 passes a `[:count]` view of a larger array and checks that the tail is unchanged. The slice's rationale relies on this guarantee (slice lines 125–127). One small test would cover it.

findings.title: Full suite runs three times
findings.description: `pytest` runs in Task 3.5 (line 240), Task 5.1 (line 292) and Task 5.2 step 2 (line 300). Task 5.1 can be merged into 5.2. The rest of the plan is a sensible size for an effort-2 slice: one task file, about 20 tasks.
